chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās and Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Deliberate killing is that he intentionally targets him and kills him with something by which the like of him is killed. Mistaken killing is that he acts deliberately but does not intend to kill him, yet kills him with something by which the like of him is not usually killed. And the mistake about which there is no doubt is that he intends something else, then strikes him.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said, may Allah be pleased with him: What we rely upon concerning the blood-money is that one hundred camels, or two hundred cattle, or one thousand sheep, or one thousand dinars, or ten thousand dirhams are binding upon the killer. Most of the narrations that we presented indicate this. As for what has been narrated, that the owner of camels, if he does not have camels with him, gives for each camel twenty head from the mature male sheep, so that they become two thousand sheep, this admits two possibilities: one of them is that camels are only binding upon the people of the desert lands, so whoever refuses to give camels, the governor compels them to give the value of each camel as twenty head from the mature male sheep, because the refusal comes from their side. But if they do not have camels, or they have sheep and are given the choice regarding it, then no more than one thousand sheep is due from them. And what clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-money compensation due in cases of homicide
key_terms.الشَّاةِ: sheep, one of the listed equivalents for diyah payment
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, one of the principal standards for assessing diyah
key_terms.الْخَطَأَ: mistaken killing where the act occurs without intent to kill, or by striking another target
key_terms.الْعَمْدَ: intentional killing done with deliberate targeting and a normally lethal means
key_terms.الْقَاتِلَ: the killer upon whom the compensation becomes binding
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: silver dirham, another monetary equivalent for diyah
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: gold dinar, a monetary equivalent for diyah

ai.seo_question: How does Shi'i hadith define intentional and accidental killing, and what is the prescribed diyah?
ai.summary: This text defines categories of homicide in legal terms: intentional killing, quasi-mistaken killing, and clear accidental killing. It also explains the relied-upon ruling regarding diyah, listing its recognized equivalents and clarifying how some variant reports about payment in sheep may be understood.
